extracted.intended_audience: SEC staff, exchange members/market participants, and legal/compliance teams reviewing or responding to exchange fee filings
extracted.subtask_description: Methodology and supporting rationale the Exchange uses to allocate costs to 10Gb ULL connectivity and Limited Service MEI Ports, set per-connection/port fees, and explain differences versus affiliated markets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Resources allocation process (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Twice a year, and as needed with additional new hires and new project initiatives, managers and department heads assign a percentage of time to every employee and then allocate that time amongst the Exchange and its affiliated markets to determine each market's individual Human Resources expense. This process ensures that every employee is 100% allocated, ensuring there is no double counting between the Exchange and its affiliated markets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocation is done in consultation with employees as needed; allocations are updated semiannually or as projects/hiring require; the goal is full (100%) allocation to avoid double-counting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Resources allocation to connectivity (network infrastructure team)
rubrics_metrics.description: For personnel whose functions include providing and maintaining physical connectivity (primarily the Exchange's network infrastructure team), the Exchange allocated a weighted average of 42.4% of each employee's time from the above group to 10Gb ULL connectivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify employees whose primary duties directly support connectivity (installation, configuration, maintenance of connections and related hardware/software, R&D for connectivity equipment/software, application support and reporting related to network performance) and apply a high-percentage allocation (example: 42.4%) to connectivity for that group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Resources allocation to ancillary personnel (smaller allocations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange allocated Human Resources costs to a limited subset of personnel with ancillary functions related to establishing and maintaining connectivity (such as information security, sales, membership, and finance personnel) on an employee-by-employee basis and applied a smaller allocation to such employees' time to 10Gb ULL connectivity (less than 20%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include only personnel with a direct nexus to connectivity tasks; compute allocations employee-by-employee and apply smaller percentages for ancillary roles (e.g., sales, billing, security).

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior executives time allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Senior level executives' time was only allocated to the 10Gb ULL connectivity related Human Resources costs to the extent that they are involved in overseeing tasks related to providing physical connectivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not broadly allocate executive compensation to connectivity unless executives are directly overseeing connectivity-related functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Resources cost calculation (blended rate)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Human Resources cost was calculated using a blended rate of compensation reflecting salary, equity and bonus compensation, benefits, payroll taxes, and 401(k) matching contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When converting allocated time into dollar cost, use a blended total-compensation rate that includes cash and non-cash compensation and benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connectivity cost driver definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Connectivity cost driver includes external fees paid to connect to other exchanges and third parties, cabling and switches required to operate the Exchange. The Connectivity cost driver is more narrowly focused on technology used to complete connections to the Exchange and to connect to external markets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify external interconnect fees, cabling, switches, and similar tangible connection costs under the connectivity driver; recognize these as necessary to receive market data and operate the matching engine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet Services and External Market Data cost driver
rubrics_metrics.description: The internet services cost driver includes third-party service providers that provide the internet, fiber and bandwidth connections between the Exchange's networks, primary and secondary data centers, and office locations. External market data includes fees paid to third parties, including other exchanges, to receive market data. The Exchange includes external market data fee costs towards the provision of 10Gb ULL connectivity because such market data is necessary for certain services related to connectivity, including pre-trade risk checks and checks for other conditions (e.g., re-pricing of orders to avoid locked or crossed markets and trading collars).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate a portion of external market data costs to connectivity when market data is consumed at the entry/matching engine level to validate orders or perform pre-trade checks; include network bandwidth/fiber fees that support connectivity between sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Center cost allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Data Center costs includes an allocation of the costs the Exchange incurs to provide physical connectivity in the third-party data centers where it maintains its equipment (such as dedicated space, security services, cooling and power). The Exchange allocated a high percentage of the Data Center cost (61.9%) to physical 10Gb ULL connectivity because the third-party data centers and the Exchange's physical equipment contained therein is the most direct cost in providing physical access to the Exchange.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate substantial Data Center costs to connectivity since leased space, power, cooling and security are direct and tangible costs of providing physical access to market participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hardware and Software Maintenance and Licenses allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Hardware and Software Licenses includes hardware and software licenses used to operate and monitor physical assets necessary to offer physical connectivity to the Exchange.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate maintenance and licensing costs for hardware and software that directly support connectivity; differences in allocation among affiliates may be driven by timing of hardware refreshes and platform-specific upgrade activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depreciation cost driver and periods
rubrics_metrics.description: All physical assets, software, and hardware used to provide 10Gb ULL connectivity were valued at cost, and depreciated or leased over periods ranging from three to five years. Depreciation cost primarily relates to servers necessary to operate the Exchange, some owned and some leased. The Exchange allocated 63.8% of its allocated depreciation costs to providing physical 10Gb ULL connectivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value assets at cost and apply depreciation schedules (e.g., 3–5 years) appropriate to the asset class; include budgeted improvements to be capitalized and depreciated when narrowly related to connectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocated Shared Expenses multi-layered allocation process
rubrics_metrics.description: General shared expenses (office space/expenses, utilities, recruiting and training, marketing/advertising, professional fees, telecommunications, board director fees, etc.) are incurred by the Exchange's parent company and allocated to the Exchange and its affiliated markets. The Exchange then allocated the general shared expense assigned to the Exchange across core services (including connectivity) and further to sub-categories (e.g., 10Gb ULL connectivity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a multi-layered allocation: (1) allocate shared corporate expenses among affiliated markets, (2) allocate the Exchange's share across core services, (3) allocate across sub-categories. Use meetings with senior management, department heads and Finance to determine reasonable allocation percentages, and ensure each expense is allocated only once.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighting allocations by core-service importance (example: 51.3% to 10Gb)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange allocated 51.3% of the portion allocated to physical connectivity to 10Gb ULL connectivity. The Exchange believes this allocation percentage is reasonable because it is based on and in line with the percentage allocations of each of the Exchange's other cost drivers and reflects the importance of 10Gb ULL connectivity to the Exchange's strategy and operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When apportioning shared connectivity costs between product offerings, weight allocations to reflect relative importance, resource usage, and alignment with other cost-driver percentages; document strategic rationale (e.g., premium product, determinism, throughput).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of quantifiable criteria for affiliate allocations
rubrics_metrics.description: This allocation methodology results in an allocation among the Exchange and its affiliated markets based on set quantifiable criteria, i.e., actual number of 10Gb ULL connections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, allocate costs across affiliated markets using objective, countable metrics (e.g., number of physical connections, number of ports, matching engines) rather than purely subjective splits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of approximate cost per 10Gb ULL connection per month
rubrics_metrics.description: After determining the approximate allocated monthly cost related to 10Gb connectivity, the total monthly cost for 10Gb ULL connectivity of $946,799 was divided by the number of physical 10Gb ULL connections the Exchange maintained at the time that proposed pricing was determined (102), to arrive at a cost of approximately $9,282 per month, per physical 10Gb ULL connection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute per-connection unit cost by dividing the total allocated monthly connectivity cost by the actual number of physical connections in the period used for pricing calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not allocate any expense in full to one core service; avoid double-counting
rubrics_metrics.description: In conducting its Cost Analysis, the Exchange did not allocate any of its expenses in full to any core services (including physical connectivity or Limited Service MEI Ports) and did not double-count any expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure shared costs are split across applicable services and documented; verify that no expense line is fully assigned to a single product when it supports multiple services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited Service MEI Ports cost-driver structure (parallel to connectivity)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Limited Service MEI Ports the Exchange considered line-item costs analogous to connectivity: Human Resources, Connectivity (external fees, cabling, switches), Internet Services and External Market Data, Data Center, Hardware and Software Maintenance and Licenses, Depreciation, and Allocated Shared Expenses. Example allocations include allocating approximately 5.9% of overall Human Resources cost to offering Limited Service MEI Ports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat port services as their own cost center but allocate using the same set of drivers as connectivity when appropriate; document per-driver percentage allocations and provide explanatory differences versus affiliates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depreciation allocation for Limited Service MEI Ports (software/hardware treatment)
rubrics_metrics.description: The vast majority of the software the Exchange uses to provide Limited Service MEI Ports has been developed in-house and the cost of such development is depreciated over time once the software is activated in the production environment. The Exchange allocated 3.7% of all depreciation costs to providing Limited Service MEI Ports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalize and depreciate in-house software development costs when placed in production; allocate a specific depreciation percentage to ports based on the software/hardware footprint attributable to port services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of approximate cost per Limited Service MEI Port per month
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on August 2023 data, the total monthly cost allocated to Limited Service MEI Ports of $148,255 was divided by the total number of Limited Service MEI Ports utilized by Members in August (1,030, including free and charged ports), resulting in an approximate cost of $144 per port per month (rounded).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When determining per-port unit cost, include both free and charged ports in the denominator if the Exchange incurs expense to maintain free ports; use recent period utilization data for calculations and round appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of free ports and pricing proposal mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange changed its proposed fee structure to offer four free Limited Service MEI Ports per matching engine (previously two), and after the first four free ports the Exchange proposes to charge $420 per Limited Service MEI Port per matching engine, up to a total of fourteen (14) ports per matching engine. The Exchange included free and charged ports when calculating per-port cost and quantified the total expense of free ports (e.g., 468 ports not charged would amount to $67,392 per month at $144 per port).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state how free-unit allowances are treated in cost calculations and show example member-level math (e.g., 12 matching engines × 14 ports = 168 total ports; 4 free per engine → 48 free ports; remainder charged). Quantify aggregate expense of free allowances when modeling revenue impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain and document differences among affiliated markets
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocation percentages for specific cost drivers and dollar amounts differ among the Exchange and its affiliated markets due to factors such as unique technical architecture, market structure, business requirements, timing of hardware refreshes, and number of matching engines (e.g., MIAX maintaining 24 matching engines vs. MIAX Emerald's 12). These differences can cause percentage allocation variances even when dollar differences are non-significant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When allocation percentages differ across affiliates, document the concrete operational reasons (architecture, port counts, matching engine counts, hardware refresh cycles) and quantify dollar differences to show materiality (or immateriality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee-by-employee allocation where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange allocated cost on an employee-by-employee basis when only including those personnel who support functions related to providing physical connectivity, and then applied smaller allocations for those employees to specific services (e.g., 10Gb ULL connectivity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For roles that only partly support a product, perform employee-level time allocations rather than broad departmental percentages; document criteria used to include or exclude employees from specific allocations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonableness confirmation via consultations and meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: The estimates of Human Resources cost were determined by consulting with department leaders, determining which employees are involved in tasks related to the service, and confirming that the proposed allocations were reasonable based on an understanding of the percentage of time such employees devote to those tasks. The Exchange also held meetings with senior management, department heads, and the Finance Team to determine the proper amount of shared general expense to allocate to 10Gb ULL connectivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use documented consultations with department heads and finance, and cross-check allocations against observable time commitments and activities to support the reasonableness of allocations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use same Cost Analysis across related fee proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange used the same Cost Analysis to form the basis of this proposal and the filings the Exchange submitted proposing fees for proprietary data feeds offered by the Exchange.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a consistent underlying cost-analysis methodology when proposing related fees (connectivity, ports, data feeds) to ensure comparability and avoid inconsistent allocations.
